name: Ninoy Aquino International Airport
before:
The main gateway to the Philippines, between Pasay and Parañaque about 7 km south of Manila proper. It is the hub for Philippine Airlines and PAL Express and the main base for Cebu Pacific and Philippines AirAsia.

Be honest with clients about the congestion. The airport handled more than 50 million passengers in 2024, a record and 47 per cent up on the year before, against a design capacity of 35 million. That overload clogs air traffic and delays flights, and the airport has consistently been named among the worst in the world. Build slack into connections here.

Change is under way. Operations and maintenance were privatised in September 2024 and handed to a consortium led by San Miguel Corporation, which is responsible for rehabilitating the airport. Two further projects, a new airport at Bulakan in Bulacan and an upgrade to Sangley Point in Cavite City, are meant to take pressure off, and Clark International already shares the Greater Manila market.

There are three passenger terminals with two more planned. Terminal 1 was designed for six million passengers a year.

The airport is named after Benigno Aquino Jr, who was assassinated here in August 1983.
after:
The Philippines' main gateway, south of central Manila. It is the hub for Philippine Airlines and PAL Express and the main base for Cebu Pacific and Philippines AirAsia.

Be honest with clients about the congestion. The airport handled a record 52 million passengers in 2025 against a design capacity of about 35 million, and it has long been called one of the world's worst airports. Build slack into connections here.

New NAIA Infra Corp, a consortium led by San Miguel Corporation, took over operations and maintenance on 14 September 2024 and is modernising the airport. Most turboprop island flights have since moved to other airports.

There are three passenger terminals, with a new Terminal 4 being built and a Terminal 5 planned. Airlines were moved between them in March 2026, with more moves planned, so check the terminal before setting off.

It was renamed after Ninoy Aquino in 1987.
